case_title: Shivani Tyagi v. State of U.P. & Anr.
aggravating_circumstances: Permanent disfiguration of the victim; acid attack; serious nature of the offence
trial_court_outcome: Convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment
high_court_outcome: Suspended the sentence and enlarged on bail
neutral_facts: The accused subjected the victim to an acid attack, resulting in severe burns to her face, chest, and hands. The victim sustained grievous injuries, leading to permanent disfigurement. The trial court convicted the accused under Sections 307/149 and 326A/149 of the IPC and sentenced them to life imprisonment. The High Court suspended the sentences and released the accused on bail, citing the offer of compensation by the accused and the potential delay in the appeal process. The Supreme Court overturned the High Court's decision, emphasizing that the serious nature of the offence and the permanent disfigurement of the victim should have been considered, and that the suspension of the sentence was not justified.
